UNITED STATES OF AMERICA 
BEFORE THE 
FEDERAL ENERGY REGULATORY COMMISSION 
PJM Governance and Stakeholder Reforms 
Docket Nos. AD26-7-000
COMMENTS OF NORTH CAROLINA ELECTRIC MEMBERSHIP 
CORPORATION 
North Carolina Electric Membership Corporation (NCEMC) submits these 
comments pursuant to the Commission’s Notice Requesting Post-Conference 
Comment of July 30, 2026.  
NCEMC is a generation and transmission cooperative responsible for the 
full or partial power supply requirements of its 25 members throughout the state of 
North Carolina. Those 25 distribution cooperatives, in turn, supply electricity to 
approximately one million homes, farms, and businesses in which more than 2.5 
million North Carolinians live and work. NCEMC distribution cooperative loads 
are located throughout the service areas of three investor-owned public utilities: 
Duke Energy Carolinas, LLC, and Duke Energy Progress, LLC, both subsidiaries 
of Duke Energy Corporation, and Virginia Electric and Power Company, doing 
business as Dominion Energy Virginia in Virginia and as Dominion Energy North 
Carolina in North Carolina (hereinafter, Dominion).  
NCEMC is a member of PJM Interconnection, L.L.C., (PJM) and a member 
of the Electric Distributor sector. NCEMC purchases transmission services from 
PJM to serve the loads of its six member cooperatives that distribute power at

2 
retail in the Dominion transmission zone of the PJM region. NCEMC also 
participates in PJM’s energy, ancillary services, capacity, and financial 
transmission rights markets.  
NCEMC has appended to these comments its responses to the questions 
posed in the appendix to the Commission’s July 30 Notice Requesting Post-
Conference Comment.

Appendix
The questions below focus on broad themes, shared concerns, or potential points of 
consensus that emerged during the technical conference.  They are not intended to be 
exhaustive, dispositive, or a comprehensive catalog of all matters relevant to governance 
and stakeholder issues.  Although these questions contain individual elements that are 
interrelated and potential changes to one element may affect others, please answer each 
question independently.  In your response, please indicate the PJM member sector to 
which your company or organization belongs, or, if you are not a PJM member, please 
indicate that.  In addition to answering the questions, the Commission welcomes post-
conference comments that provide any additional information, perspectives, or proposals 
that market participants believe will best facilitate reforms to PJM’s governance structure 
and stakeholder processes.   
PJM Board Independence 
Questions/Comments 
Yes
No
1) 
Should Board members’ terms be extended to five or more years? 
Comments: Depending on the totality of the PJM reforms implemented during 
this reform process, NCEMC could support Board members’ terms being 
extended to five years. 
2) 
Should there be a maximum number of years that a Board member 
may serve (e.g., 10 years)? 
X 
Comments: At this point in time, NCEMC does not support term limits. 
3) 
Should the Board member qualification rules be revised to provide a 
preference for some Board members that reside in the PJM region? 
Comments: At this point in time, NCEMC does not support a residency 
requirement for Board members; that said, NCEMC has no objection to exploring 
revision of the Board member qualification rules to include a residency 
preference where all else is equal between candidates. 
4) 
Should the conflict-of-interest rules be revised to reduce the cooling 
off period for Board members from two years to one year? 
X 
Comments:  
5) 
Should restrictions on Board communications be relaxed to enable 
more communication between the Board and stakeholders? 
X

4 
Questions/Comments 
Yes
No
Comments: NCEMC would support relaxed restrictions on Board 
communications that are made to all stakeholders in a fair and impartial manner; 
at this time, NCEMC does not support relaxing any restrictions that would 
sanction unconstrained ex parte communications.  
6) 
In order to increase transparency, should Board votes be made public 
or the Board be required to explain its reasoning?  
X 
Comments:  
7) 
In order to increase transparency, should some Board meetings be 
open or available to the public? 
X 
Comments:   
8) 
Should PJM’s governing documents be revised to explicitly state that 
the responsibility of PJM and its Board is to serve the public interest? 
X 
Comments:  
9) 
Should state representatives have at least one voting member on the 
Nominating Committee? 
X 
Comments:  
10) 
Should PJM adopt public performance metrics and tie management 
compensation to their achievement? 
Comments: At this time, NCEMC takes no position on this question other than 
observing that – on information and belief – PJM may already use performance 
assessment metrics to evaluate staff and adjust compensation. 
Section 205 Filing Rights 
Questions/Comments 
Yes
No
11) 
Should the stakeholder process be advisory, i.e., stakeholder votes 
only inform the Board? 
X 
Comments:

Questions/Comments 
Yes

12) 
Should PJM have section 205 filing rights over the energy market and 
ancillary services unencumbered by the requirement to obtain 
approval of two-thirds of the Members Committee? 
Comments: PJM stakeholders, including NCEMC, are actively discussing the 
“Section 205 Filing Rights” questions. At this time, NCEMC does not support 
PJM having Section 205 filing rights in non-exigent circumstances or in 
circumstances where the stakeholder process is advancing toward consensus. 
13) 
Should PJM have section 205 filing rights over Regional 
Transmission Expansion Planning (RTEP) unencumbered by the 
requirement to obtain approval of two-thirds of the Members 
Committee? 
Comments:  PJM stakeholders, including NCEMC, are actively discussing the 
“Section 205 Filing Rights” questions. At this time, NCEMC does not support 
PJM having Section 205 filing rights in non-exigent circumstances or in 
circumstances where the stakeholder process is advancing toward consensus. 
14) 
Should the Organization of PJM States Inc (OPSI) have “jump ball” 
rights over resource adequacy and transmission cost allocation filings 
when a supermajority of OPSI agrees on an alternative proposal? 
Comments: PJM stakeholders, including NCEMC, are actively discussing the 
“Section 205 Filing Rights” questions. 
15) 
Should the Members Committee have “jump ball” filing rights over 
the portions of the tariff where PJM has 205 filing rights when a 
supermajority of stakeholders approves an alternative proposal? 
Comments: PJM stakeholders, including NCEMC, are actively discussing the 
“Section 205 Filing Rights” questions.

State Participation 
Questions/Comments 
Yes
No
18) 
In addition to OPSI, should there be a second state representative 
group consisting of governors’ representatives and/or state legislators’ 
representatives? 
Comments: At this time, NCEMC supports enhanced state participation in the 
PJM stakeholder process. That said, NCEMC is not convinced that a second state 
representative group, in addition to OPSI is needed. NCEMC supports the 
following proposal put forward by PJM: “PJM proposes to increase state 
participation in PJM in two ways. First, PJM will work with the states to enhance 
OPSI to include in a bicameral structure for both the state commissions and the 
executive branches of each state. It is important that each state speak with one 
voice through OPSI. PJM would support increased funding for the reconstituted 
OPSI, recognizing not only the addition of the executive branch, but also the 
need for greater engagement in the stakeholder process. Second, PJM proposes to 
revise the stakeholder process to allow for OPSI to make a proposal on equal 
footing with any Member proposal or any PJM proposal, each in the area of 
resource adequacy, at any stage in the stakeholder process.” 
19) 
Should state representatives have a formal voting role in the 
stakeholder process (limited to certain topics, such as resource 
adequacy and regional transmission cost allocation) in addition to the 
consumer advocate votes?   
Comments: At this time, NCEMC supports giving OPSI a formal informational 
vote at a minimum and NCEMC is open to exploring the concept of affording 
OPSI a more formal vote that is more than merely informational. 
20) 
Should PJM be required to consult with OPSI prior to making a 
section 205 filing related to resource adequacy and transmission cost 
allocation? 
X
